Command: Offer the daily burnt offerings morning and evening
Summary: The command: Offer the daily burnt offerings morning and evening (Numbers 28:3). Two lambs of the first year, without spot, were offered day by day continually, one in the morning and one in the evening.
Commandment: Offer the daily burnt offerings morning and evening, as prescribed in Numbers 28:3.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: Two lambs without spot, one in the morning and one in the evening, day by day continually — a ceremonial law of unbroken offering. Its goal was to keep atonement and worship going every single day, the nation's offering never pausing. It did not address a particular evil; its work was constancy, not restraint. Morning and evening, the lambs went up, and Israel's days were framed by sacrifice from first light to last.
